title: Token-cohort asymmetric quantization probe for KV store to optimize GPU residency
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: evaluate a token-cohort aware asymmetric quantization scheme for KV cache activations to reduce GPU memory footprint while bounding quality regression across long-context workloads. This probe focuses on per-cohort scaling, an asymmetric zero-point to reduce bias for low-variance subtokens, and a runtime fallback to higher-fidelity representations for cohorts that show degradation. The work ties into continuous batching and GPU memory defragmentation by enabling more aggressive packing of KV shards and reducing peak residency during bursts.
acceptance_criteria: Design and implement an asymmetric quant codec for KV vectors supporting INT4/INT8/FP8 output paths in the runtime
Automated pipeline that samples token cohorts during inference and selects quant profiles based on their dynamic range and SNR
Quality regression on held-out benchmarks (long-context summarization, multi-turn chat) < 2% token-level degradation for INT8, <6% for INT4, compared to FP16 baseline

End-to-end GPU memory reduction measured on p4d/p3-like instances: >=18% reduction in KV residency for INT8 mode, >=34% for INT4 mode, without violating latency SLOs in 95th percentile under continuous batching workloads
Fallback policy (cohort uplift) implemented to transparently rehydrate selected KV cohorts to FP16 when quality triggers are breached
Bench artifacts (scripts, dashboards, PRs) linked in ticket and reproducible by infra team
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Data collection - run 100K inference requests across 4 representative workloads (LLM-chat, long-document QA, code-assist, summarization) to build token-cohort statistics (range, skew, burstiness)
Phase 1: Offline quant encoder - implement per-cohort asymmetric linear quantization with learned zero-point and scale; support INT4/INT8/FP8 packing with block sizes 16/32
Phase 2: Microbench - perf test codec kernels on CUDA (A100) and measure encode/decode costs, throughput impact under continuous batching scenarios
Phase 3: KV store integration - integrate encoder into runtime KV write path and decoder into read path; add metadata for cohort ID and quant profile
Phase 4: Canary rollout - enable INT8 adaptive mode on 5% of production traffic (internal staging) with logging for quality metrics and fallback triggers
Phase 5: Stress tests - run sustained burst workloads with synthetic long contexts to measure 95/99p latency and memory residency
Phase 6: Analysis - compute quality deltas (perplexity, token-error), memory savings, and failure modes; iterate on profile selectors and fallback thresholds
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with serving runtime, infra, and eval teams. Agreed on target workloads and initial cohort definition (by token type + relative frequency).

2025-02-20: Collected 100K inference traces from staging harness and produced token-cohort stats. Observed heavy tail of low-variance subtokens (punctuation/stopwords) suitable for aggressive compression.
2025-02-26: Prototype asymmetric encoder implemented in C++ CUDA kernel (encode/decode). Preliminary microbench: encode+decode adds ~1.6us per KV write/read on A100 for block size 32 in INT8 path.
2025-03-01: Offline quality sweep: INT8 asymmetric on held-out summarization set shows median token-perplexity delta +0.8%, worst-case +1.9% on rare-cohort texts; INT4 median +3.9%, worst-case +7.2%.

2025-03-04: Integrated lightweight cohort metadata into KV headers. Added simple runtime fallback funnel (threshold-based) that marks cohorts for rehydration when reconstruction error > 6e-3 L2 relative.
2025-03-05: Canary plan drafted; waiting on infra quota for staging GPUs to run 72h canary under continuous batching config.
results_summary: Early results indicate asymmetric INT8 provides a strong memory/quality trade-off: ~20-22% KV residency reduction with quality within the 2% target for most workloads. INT4 yields larger memory reduction (~36%) but has tail cases where token-level degradation exceeds the 6% threshold, especially for low-frequency technical tokens and long-range dependencies. The asymmetric zero-point reduced systematic bias versus symmetric quant for punctuation-heavy cohorts. Kernel overhead is acceptable for most continuous-batching SLOs; worst-case p95 latency uplift is +4-6% during encode-heavy bursts.
notes: Key trade-off: cohort granularity increases metadata overhead; we balance by using hashed cohort IDs and grouping low-frequency tokens together.
Fallback policy needs to consider cost: rehydrating too often defeats memory savings. We plan to add a cooldown and a budget for rehydrates per request-window.
Edge case: decoder numerics under FP8 path showed variance across CUDA architectures. We added cross-architecture unit tests to the CI.
Follow-up: run human evals on chat flows to surface subjective regressions not captured by token metrics.
